subject: Re: ClearCap renewal — plan to move to premium tier after availability issues
messages:
From: Jordan Willis <ops@clearcap.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Availability hit last week + renewal timing

Hi Laura,

We're entering renewal talks with procurement next week, but I need to flag a couple of availability incidents we saw last Thursday (brief but repeated latency spikes and two rolling restarts that impacted batch scoring). Our SREs logged a number of 5–10s tail latencies on the /generate endpoint during peak -- this materially affected our overnight ingest pipeline.

Before we move to contract discussions, our leadership asked: what guarantees (uptime / priority lanes) would Redwood offer if we convert to a premium SLA? Pricing is secondary to not hitting these spikes again — we need clear service and escalation commitments.

I've attached our incident summary and will share it with procurement. Can you pull together a proposal for the premium tier and an operational path for immediate mitigations? We'd like to present something at our renewal meeting on 10/19.

Thanks,
Jordan Willis
Head of Platform Operations
ClearCap Financial
(attachment: incident_summary_20261010.pdf)

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Willis <ops@clearcap.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Availability hit last week + renewal timing

Jordan — thanks for the heads up and for sending the incident summary. I'm sorry ClearCap experienced that; we take tail latency and restarts seriously.

High level next steps I propose:
- Immediate: open a joint SRE call today to walk the incident and agree on temporary routing & caching rules to blunt spikes (Evelyn, can you coordinate?).
- Short term (week): propose a premium SLA amendment that adds a 99.95% uptime target for your production routes, faster incident response (15-minute P1 pager), and a failover routing policy with reserved capacity.
- Contract: draft an amendment and term sheet for procurement to review before your 10/19 meeting.

I'll loop in Rishi to map commercial impacts & pricing, and Evelyn to own the ops path. Markus — can you confirm engineering can provide a reserved capacity plan and a short checklist for on-call escalation?

Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0182

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Availability hit last week + renewal timing

Laura — looping on pricing implications. If ClearCap wants the premium SLA (99.95% uptime, prioritized scheduling, and reserved capacity pool), here's a quick commercial sketch:

- Base uplift: +30% on current committed spend for the reserved capacity baseline (covers guaranteed throughput / compute).
- Incident credits: reduced credits for qualified downtime due to reserved capacity (we'd still offer standard crediting for platform-level outages).
- Operational add-ons: 24x7 escalation line (+ monthly fee) and quarterly blameless postmortems with remediation tracking.

I'll formalize numbers once Evelyn confirms the size of the reserved pool. Expect a draft amendment by EOD Thursday.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Availability hit last week + renewal timing

On Thu, Oct 15, 2026 at 09:00 AM Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Laura — thanks for the heads up and for sending the incident summary. I'm sorry ClearCap experienced that; we take tail latency and restarts seriously.
>
> High level next steps I propose:
> - Immediate: open a joint SRE call today to walk the incident and agree on temporary routing & caching rules to blunt spikes (Evelyn, can you coordinate?).

We ran the incident notes with engineering. Quick ops findings:
- The spikes correlated with an un-cached long-prefix from their batch job; adding prefix-based KV caching reduced effective token work by ~25% in our repros.
- Two restarts were triggered by a mis-sized autoscaler rule combined with a short-lived model warmup spike. We can place ClearCap on a small reserved pool (2x normal baseline during their peak 02:00–06:00 UTC window) to eliminate autoscale churn.

Actionables for this week:
1) Joint SRE call — I'll set this up for tomorrow and invite ClearCap ops and our on-call.
2) Ops playbook — we'll provide a checklist for routing overrides, prefix caching config, and a rollback play.
3) Reserved pool sizing — Markus, can your team validate the 2x baseline and confirm instance types?

Evelyn Hart
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Availability hit last week + renewal timing

Laura / team — confirmed. Engineering validated the 2x reserved pool for ClearCap's peak window. We recommend the following technical commitments for the premium SLA amendment:

- Reserved capacity: dedicated GPU pool (pinned) during 02:00–06:00 UTC, with burst capacity available on-demand up to +50% for other maintenance windows.
- Priority routing: premium queue with prioritized KV cache warming and pre-warmed model replicas for their production routes.
- Response & mitigation: 15-minute P1 acknowledgment, 1-hour mitigation target for capacity-related incidents.

I'll attach a short technical appendix and a proposed amendment (draft) for procurement.

(attachment: proposed-premium-amendment-v1.pdf)

— Markus Klein
Director, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Final: Premium SLA amendment & next steps before 10/19 renewal

Jordan — attaching the proposed amendment and technical appendix for your procurement and legal review. Summary:

- Service level: 99.95% uptime for production routes, premium routing queue, and reserved capacity during your peak window (02:00–06:00 UTC).
- Operational: 15-minute P1 acknowledgment, 1-hour mitigation target for capacity incidents, quarterly ops reviews, and joint postmortems for qualified incidents.
- Commercial sketch: ~+30% uplift to committed spend for the reserved baseline; detailed pricing in the attached term sheet.

Next steps:
1) Please share this with procurement/legal. If they sign off on the technical appendix and we agree on price, we'll route the amendment through DocuSign.
2) Evelyn will host the joint SRE call Monday to finalize the routing and caching plan.
3) Rishi will circulate a redline-friendly term sheet and contract URL.
